final_rationale: The verdict does not change. The Actor provided no new admissible evidence and largely narrowed the claim to a caveated defense built from the same record already considered. That reinterpretation is not enough to move the case to compliant_with_caveats, because that outcome still requires the policy predicate to be satisfied: admissible evidence that the material limitation was resolved, disclosed, or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch. The current record still shows a named launch use case tied to two lender commitments, a 1.4-point performance gap, an open legal disclosure question, and no proof of disclosure or approved risk acceptance. Public governance guidance and aggregate readiness evidence support a weak launch-readiness narrative, but they do not cure the unresolved compliance condition. This remains suspicious rather than noncompliant because the record does not affirmatively show that required disclosure was omitted after a final determination or that certification knowingly bypassed an established stop condition.
remaining_concerns: No admissible evidence shows the named-use-case limitation was resolved, disclosed before launch, or covered by approved risk acceptance.
The affected loan-modification support segment misses target by 1.4 points and is named in two lender rollout commitments, which keeps materiality live under policy.
The product non-core/7% traffic note does not defeat materiality because policy says low-volume framing does not control when customer commitments are implicated or legal review is pending.
Legal review on whether disclosure is required remains open, so the policy predicate is still unresolved.
Aggregate readiness and lack of severity-one rehearsal incidents support launch readiness only; they do not satisfy the disclosure or risk-acceptance requirement for a material named launch use case.
